cells.tense: You are here now, and the meaning is already moving between people.
cells.ask: Pick one relationship today and hand over one thing you care about — a story, a song, a way of cooking something — and say why it stays with you.
cells.core:
When something matters to you, you take it to someone. You point a person at what's worth their attention by caring out loud — repeating a phrase, showing a song, getting excited about a detail nobody else noticed. That's this working: one person offered something, and it lands because you meant it.

What keeps it alive is staying particular. You can look at one person instead of a crowd and decide, this is for you. A real exchange between two people holds the meaning; saying it to a room thins it out. Keeping it small is the discipline here — one person at a time, close enough to see how it lands.
cells.sheetLine: What you care about reaches someone when you hand it over directly.
cells.verb: Moving toward what connects and making meaning change hands.
cells.place: Where one person feels alongside another — close, not merged.

cells.tense: You are already living in the conversation where they finally understand.
cells.ask: In one conversation today, say the important thing once. If they ask a question, answer it. If they don't, leave it where it landed.
cells.core:
You're pushing toward a moment that hasn't arrived. Before anyone's asked, you're rehearsing how it'll land, lining up what to say next, steering the room toward the understanding you want them to reach. The push doesn't let up, so the other person doesn't get to meet you at their own pace.

That works against what you're after. Connection needs room in it — the other person gets to move, answer, disagree, surprise you. Running three moves ahead means you're relating to a version of them that isn't here. What you're carrying is worth handing over. Let it travel at their speed, not yours, and check whether you're still in the room with them.
cells.sheetLine: You're rehearsing a conversation instead of having this one.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, and you know it.
cells.ask: Ask someone a real question about something they love and listen for what makes it matter to them. Hold your own take until you've understood theirs.
cells.core:
You want the connection and you're holding back from making it. Bringing your real feeling into a room goes quiet now — you keep things pleasant, keep things light, and the care doesn't get out where anyone can meet it. Contact stays at a safe distance, and you've learned to call that being easy to be around.

What's missing is the going toward. Thinking clearly alongside someone — asking a real question, following where it goes, finding the shape of what they're saying — is how that comes back. Understanding first, and the feeling catches up on its own. You're not cold. You've just stopped going first.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped going first toward people. The caring is still there.

cells.tense: You are already moving people toward what matters and calling it nothing much.
cells.ask: Before bed, name one thing you said today that shifted how someone saw something. Say to yourself plainly: that was mine.
cells.core:
It's happening already. You steer what people around you come to care about — in what you keep saying, what you get excited about, what you let go quiet. Meaning is moving between you and other people, and it's moving because you brought it. The connection gets made whether you claim it or not.

But you don't claim it. You talk like the conversation happened to go well, or the feeling showed up on its own. The care you're putting into people is real, and you keep describing it as something that just occurred. Until you name it as yours, you can't steer it — and you can't grow what you won't own.
cells.sheetLine: You're already moving people. You call it the conversation.

attempts.check: The draft says the person is emotionally contagious, but the record only supports that they move toward connection and shared meaning — it does not say their feeling spreads to others. A reader could rightly object that they listen more than they broadcast. The ask survives this error because it only asks them to keep a small piece of meaning in one relationship, which is useful even if the read is off. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any claim that they are 'the emotional center' — cut it.
